sector_model: advertising-funded consumer internet platform: judged on revenue growth, user (DAUq) trend and ARPU, GAAP net income and tax status, free cash flow with and without stock compensation, net cash, buyback offset of dilution, search-referral dependence; no debt, so solvency is a liquidity check; EV/revenue is context only
thesis: Reddit (NYSE: RDDT) is an ad-funded community platform. Q3 2026 revenue 895.0M (+53%), 9M 2,363.3M vs 1,476.9M (+60%); ad pricing +34%, ARPU 6.87 (+36%); gross margin 91.5%; Q3 GAAP net income 283.3M (+74%), 9M 740.1M vs 278.1M; operating income 9M 676.2M vs 210.2M. Q3 operating cash flow 363.8M, FCF 362.6M; 9M FCF 934.5M (OCF 937.9M less capex 3.5M). TTM (FY2025 plus 9M 2026 minus 9M 2025): revenue 3,088.9M, net income 991.7M, OCF 1,204.7M, capex 6.6M, FCF 1,198.1M. At the verified 2026-11-10 close of 98.67 and 193.09M Class A plus Class B shares (cover, 2026-10-28) market cap is about 19.05B: 19.2x TTM GAAP net income, FCF yield 6.3%; after TTM stock compensation of about 385.8M (FY2025 343.2M plus 9M 2026 300.6M minus 9M 2025 258.0M) FCF is about 812M, a 4.3% yield. Cash and marketable securities 3.03B and no debt (total liabilities 380.3M). Guidance for Q4 2026: revenue 1,000 to 1,030M (about +38% to +42% against 725.6M implied by FY2025 less 9M 2025) and adjusted EBITDA 480 to 510M. The stock fell from 129.60 (10-29 close) to 91.73 (10-30, -29.2%) after the release and has since recovered to 98.67. What the 10-Q shows that may explain it: global DAUq +12% y/y but flat q/q, United States DAUq -2% y/y and -5% q/q, logged-in United States DAUq about +1%, and an explicit risk factor that search engine and AI summary changes cut referral traffic in the current quarter. The market may be pricing a growth ceiling on users; the filing shows monetization (price per ad +34%) is doing the work. Cause of the drop is from the filing only; the call and analyst commentary were not read.
counterthesis: Growth is price-led: ad price +34% and ARPU +36% against DAUq +12%, with US DAUq shrinking, and the company says search and AI-summary traffic changes may continue or worsen; an advertiser pullback or a Google ranking change would hit a business with 91.5% gross margin and heavy fixed costs. Revenue growth guided from 53% to about 40% in Q4. GAAP profit is flattered: income tax was only 11.5M on 751.6M pre-tax income (1.5%) because of a full US valuation allowance, so tax-normalized earnings at 21% are about 790M and the P/E about 24x (own approximation); the allowance release will create a one-time gain that must not be treated as earnings. Stock compensation is large (300.6M in 9M; SBC and related taxes 322.1M excluded from adjusted EBITDA), so FCF yield after SBC is 4.3% rather than 6.3%. Buybacks (340.0M in 9M, 660.0M remaining) offset part of the dilution; net share count rose in 2026 anyway (Class A plus B 190.9M at 12/31/2025 to 193.1M at 9/30/2026). Data licensing (other revenue 48.0M in Q3, 130.0M in 9M, 5.5% of revenue) is small and depends on AI customers; scraping and AI-answer substitutes are named risks. Cloud commitments of 880M (AWS) and 580M (Google) run to 2029. Advance Magazine Publishers holds about 22% and the dual class structure leaves public holders limited influence. Competition from Google, Meta, TikTok, Pinterest, Snap, and AI assistants.
invalidation: US DAUq declining by more than about 5% y/y or logged-in users turning negative; ad price growth falling below about 15% while impressions do not offset; revenue growth guided below about 25%; further search-referral losses; a data-licensing contract not renewed; operating margin falling below about 20% (Q3 29%); buybacks ceasing while SBC rises.
